decisions.question: Do Spec §7.2 'Scope timing' and Spec §2.1 'Replay timing' govern nidana.navigation, although landing L1 names only §3.13 for it and landing L2 does not name the node?

options.label: add §7.2 'Scope timing' only
options.consequence: the bootstrap order the node owns and nidana.navigation.6's tests trace to the rule that admits an APPLICATION resolver before start() and requires a PAGE topology after it; §2.1 stays out

options.label: add both §7.2 and §2.1
options.consequence: also names when a new subscriber receives its replay, which bus-api@v2 G17, G22 and G34 state and navigation reads only through them

options.label: add neither
options.consequence: keeps the Sources rule read narrowly (only landings that name the node), and leaves the scope-timing reliance of the bootstrap order and of G16's PAGE picker without a source

decisions.why: The bootstrap order activates the resolver before start(), which bus-api@v2 G42 admits only because it is APPLICATION-scoped; the executor claims through a publisher, which G42 admits at any time; and G16's PAGE picker must be activated after start(). H5 checked both suites against §7.2 (S62: no change), so L2 reached this node through its contract. §2.1 'Replay timing' governs when a subscriber receives its first value: the executor subscribes to an event topic, which does not replay, and the resolver's reads connect as G34 and G22 state, so navigation reads §3.13's order, not §2.1. Close call: a strict reading of the Sources rule (landings whose Reaches list names the node) drops §7.2. A navigation guarantee or phase that depended on replay timing after start() would have added §2.1.

decisions.question: Does the Owns bullet on the deep-link bootstrap order ('the resolver is active and the executor constructed before start()') stay word for word, or is it restated for Spec §3.13 as v0.15.1 rewrote it?

options.label: keep the bullet
options.consequence: stays true (bus-api@v2 G34 connects the activations 'still active' at start()), but names no reliance, so a reader can assume the bus-api@v1 reading of a connection before activate returns

options.label: restate the bullet
options.consequence: names scope timing's admission of the APPLICATION resolver and the executor's publisher, that neither connects before start(), and start()'s order: the resolver after the topologies that write its inputs, then the executor's subscription, then the queued deep link; cites bus-api@v2 G34 and G42 and navigation-api@v1 Refinement 8 and G24

decisions.why: H13 names this bullet. S60 and S62 report that the bootstrap reliance moved from bus-api@v1 G22 and G34 to bus-api@v2 G34 alone, and the inserted phase-plan step and hsdd-config read the header. G24 holds unchanged on the v2 stand-in, so the restatement changes what the bullet cites, not the order the node owns.

decisions.question: Does the header carry navigation-api@v1 G13's new clause (the resolver's stage functions built once per navResolver call, so re-activation under bus-api@v2 G23 returns the handle, and another call's topology conflicts), or is it left to D5, which the phase plan wrote?

options.label: leave it to D5
options.consequence: the header says nothing of re-activation until the inserted phase-plan step restates D5, and the Sources' Spec §3.9 and Guide §6.3 trace to no header item

options.label: add it to the resolver's Owns bullet
options.consequence: the Owns list names a guarantee this node produces and whose replay changed; the Isolation strategy says the resolver is tested through its recorded IR and its plans, where the new G13 case compares the stage functions without a bus

decisions.chosen: add it to the resolver's Owns bullet
decisions.why: S62 added the clause to G13, a guarantee of the contract this node produces, and its new case changes the replay of nidana.navigation.3 and .6 (the insert rule, DEC-775). The Owns list is where the node states what it delivers. D5 stays plan-written and goes to the inserted phase-plan step.

decisions.question: The Overview says the resolver topology 'guards and resolves' intents, Guide §3.4's order, which navigation-api@v1 Refinement 3 reverses. Is the sentence restated?

options.label: keep the sentence
options.consequence: names both duties without a stated order, but in the order Refinement 3 rejects because a deep link would bypass the guard

options.label: restate the sentence
options.consequence: reads 'resolves them and then guards them', matching Refinement 3, G13's edge order and G14

decisions.why: The S64 touch rule (DEC-804) restates a sentence that restates another artifact's guarantee falsely, and this step's done-when requires every non-plan sentence to be true under navigation-api@v1. The sentence predates Refinement 3 (S02) and v0.15.1 did not cause it.

Before this touch no non-plan sentence relied on a connection before activate returns. The old bootstrap bullet did not say so, and the restated one cites G34.
D1 TO D6 ARE ALL PLAN-WRITTEN (S32, commit b8137e4). This touch leaves them, and everything from ## Phase Plan on, byte-identical. All of it goes to the inserted hsdd-phase-plan step (DEC-775).

INSERT RULE (confirmed, already applied by DEC-775): H5 (S62) changed G13's behavior. One new case pins that the plans of one navResolver call hold == stage functions and that another call's hold its own. It is replayed by nidana.navigation.3's gate (its --guarantee list already holds G13) and by nidana.navigation.6's unrestricted replay. G14 and G24 did not change behavior (S62 T5).

FOR THE INSERTED PHASE-PLAN STEP, plan lines that cite a superseded version or that a landing contradicts (line numbers as the file now stands): (1) D3 third bullet, line 93: 'nidana.runtime's gates read bus-api@v1's bus_activation_test.dart the same way' becomes bus-api@v2; the empty-binding rule it relies on is ADR-001 item 9, unchanged. (2) D3 sixth bullet, line 96: 'flutter-binding@v1's binding of the executor suite' becomes flutter-binding@v2. (3) D5, lines 112 to 122: must say that navResolver builds its stage objects once per call, outside the declaration body (the topology() form runs its body on every planOf call), so the value one call returns re-activates to its handle under bus-api@v2 G23 and another call's throws TopologyConflict. D5's evidence (docs/auto-run/experiments/navigation-stage-names/) built them inside the declaration, which fails the new G13 case; cite docs/auto-run/experiments/navigation-api-v0151/ T4 and P5. Add as alternatives 'built inside the declaration' (conflicts with its own second activation) and 'canonicalized per configuration in a static cache' (fails the case). Sources now hold Spec §3.9 and Guide §6.3. (4) D6, line 126: 'which bus-api@v1 G18 sends to the provider zone's uncaught-error handler' becomes bus-api@v2 G18: the uncaught-error handler of the zone in which the executor's subscription listened, the zone its constructor ran in. Both of D6's error paths then reach one zone, and the executor goes on handling later intents (navigation-api-v0151 P6; Spec §10.2 third bullet of principle 5; ADR-003 item 2 as amended). (5) nidana.navigation.1 Consumes, line 159: topology-dsl@v1 and bus-api@v1 become v2. (6) nidana.navigation.1 Dependencies, line 167: 'topology-dsl@v1 declarations', 'bus-api@v1 declarations' and 'bus-testing@v1's' become v2. (8) nidana.navigation.3 Scope, line 186: add that the stage objects are built once per navResolver call, outside the declaration body, and that the phase delivers G13's new case; its Verification may add re-activation of one resolver value. (9) nidana.navigation.6 Consumes, line 219: topology-dsl@v1, bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1 become v2. The bootstrap test (deep link before the activation, then start()) is unchanged (S62 T5).
